question: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE months AS (
    SELECT 0 as month_num
    UNION ALL
    SELECT month_num + 1 FROM months WHERE month_num < 11
),
month_dates AS (
    SELECT month_num + 1 as step_num,
           DATE '2019-01-01' + (month_num * INTERVAL '1 month') as mth
    FROM months
),
base AS (
    SELECT 
        p.product_id,
        0 as step_num,
        '2018-12-01' as mth,
        it.qty as ending_inv
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM product_minimums) p
    JOIN inventory_totals it ON p.product_id = it.product_id
),
inventory_model AS (
    SELECT 
        b.product_id,
        b.step_num,
        b.mth,
        b.ending_inv
    FROM base b
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        im.product_id,
        im.step_num + 1,
        md.mth,
        CASE 
            WHEN im.ending_inv - mb.qty < pm.qty_minimum 
            THEN im.ending_inv - mb.qty + pm.qty_purchase
            ELSE im.ending_inv - mb.qty
        END as ending_inv
    FROM inventory_model im
    JOIN month_dates md ON im.step_num + 1 = md.step_num
    JOIN monthly_budget mb ON im.product_id = mb.product_id AND md.mth = mb.mth
    JOIN product_minimums pm ON im.product_id = pm.product_id
    WHERE im.step_num < 12
)
SELECT * FROM inventory_model ORDER BY product_id, step_num
